title: A mixing heteroduplex mobility assay (mHMA) to genotype homozygous mutants with small indels generated by CRISPR-Cas9 nucleases
author: Foster, Glover, et al.

steps.title: Extract genomic DNA
steps.instruction: Collect a tail‑fin clip or embryo, perform alkali lysis and neutralization, and obtain at least 50 ng of genomic DNA for each sample.

steps.title: Set up PCR amplification
steps.instruction: Prepare a 12.5 µL PCR reaction using NEB iTaq 2× Master Mix and the optimized primer pair for the CRISPR target.

substeps.instruction: Include at least one heterozygous G1 parent as a positive control.

steps.title: Denature and renature amplicons
steps.instruction: Place PCR tubes in a thermocycler, heat to 95 °C for 2 min, then cool to 25 °C at 0.1 °C / s (or use a boiling water bath that cools on the benchtop) to allow heteroduplex formation.

steps.title: Prepare polyacrylamide gel
steps.instruction: Assemble a 6–8 % TBE polyacrylamide gel (pre‑cast or hand‑cast) in an electrophoresis chamber and fill the chamber with 1× TBE running buffer.

steps.title: Load samples with dye
steps.instruction: Mix 1 µL DNA loading dye with 1–2 µL of each denatured/renatured PCR sample, then load into individual wells; reserve lanes for a DNA ladder, a heterozygous G1 positive control, a wild‑type positive control, and a no‑template control (NTC).

substeps.instruction: Do not discard the remaining denatured/renatured PCR; it will be used later for mixing HMA.

steps.title: Run electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Connect the chamber to a power supply and run the gel at 150 V for 45–60 min, stopping when the loading dye has completely migrated off the gel.

steps.title: Post‑stain gel
steps.instruction: Stain the gel for 5–10 min with ethidium bromide or an alternative nucleic‑acid stain.

steps.title: Image gel
steps.instruction: Capture the gel image using a UV transilluminator or other UV imaging system.

steps.title: Interpret initial HMA
steps.instruction: Identify heterozygous F1 organisms by the presence of heteroduplex bands (upper and/or lower bands); homozygous wild‑type or mutant individuals show a single band.

steps.title: Select single‑band F1 samples
steps.instruction: From the initial HMA, collect the denatured/renatured PCR samples of all F1 individuals that displayed a single band (potential homozygotes).

steps.title: Mix with wild‑type amplicon
steps.instruction: In a new PCR tube, combine the F1 single‑band amplicon with a known wild‑type amplicon in a 1:1 volume ratio (e.g., 2 µL each). If many F1 samples are being tested, prepare additional wild‑type amplicon as needed.

steps.title: Denature and renature mixture
steps.instruction: Subject the mixed amplicons to the same denaturation (95 °C, 2 min) and slow renaturation (cool to 25 °C at 0.1 °C / s) protocol used in step 3.

steps.title: Run mixed samples on gel
steps.instruction: Load the mixed‑sample PCR (with loading dye) onto a 6–8 % TBE polyacrylamide gel and run electrophoresis under the same conditions as steps 4–6; optionally load the original single‑band F1 amplicon side‑by‑side for direct comparison.

steps.title: Determine homozygous status
steps.instruction: Compare band patterns: if the mixture shows heteroduplex bands (multiple bands) the original F1 was a homozygous mutant; if it remains a single band, the original F1 was homozygous wild‑type.
